claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
A temperature- and strain-rate-sensitive switch between dislocation glide and deformation-induced nano-twinning governs the strength–ductility balance in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Low temperatures and high strain rates inhibit dislocation mobility in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Low temperatures and high strain rates increase deformation-induced nano-twin formation in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Deformation-induced nano-twinning contributes to sustained strain hardening and preservation of ductility at low temperature.
Nano-twins act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
At higher temperatures or lower strain rates, enhanced dislocation mobility suppresses nano-twinning and produces conventional dislocation-glide-dominated plastic flow.
The relevant nano-twins form along dislocation slip bands under dynamic loading.
Under low-temperature, high-strain-rate loading, Co-free FeNiCrMn will develop a higher nano-twin density than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Under low-temperature, high-strain-rate loading, Co-free FeNiCrMn will show a more pronounced nonlinear strain-hardening response than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Under low-temperature, high-strain-rate loading, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have higher yield strength than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Under low-temperature, high-strain-rate loading, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have improved post-yield strain hardening relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi can exist as a single-phase FCC solid solution.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the alloys remain single-phase solid solutions without precipitation or phase separation.
The proposed mechanism is most relevant from cryogenic to moderate temperatures, where thermal activation is low enough for deformation-induced twinning.
The proposed mechanism requires strain rates high enough to inhibit full dislocation relaxation.

Failure to observe either a statistically significant nano-twin-density increase or a distinctly altered strain-hardening rate in Co-free FeNiCrMn relative to CoCrFeMnNi under low-temperature, high-rate loading would falsify the proposed mechanism.
